from_speaker: Blackwell GPUs didn’t make it cheaper
our_interpretation: This combines a historical assertion about Blackwell with an indefinite forecast about Rubin. Neither part should be silently substituted for the other.
The ordinary reading of cheaper is a lower cost to perform comparable AI work, holding output quality and service requirements reasonably constant.
The surrounding discussion concerns hardware and operating costs. Aggregate industry spending and advertised API prices alone do not settle that reading.

For the historical component, benchmark measurements combined with stated ownership-cost assumptions can establish evidence of improving unit economics. Settling the Rubin forecast early requires a documented deployed-workload cost comparison.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable workload evidence supports the historical Blackwell assertion if its costs did not fall. No finite period without Rubin savings establishes the indefinite negative forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable Blackwell cost reduction contradicts the historical component. A documented Rubin deployment that lowers comparable workload costs contradicts the forecast.
